skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Creates isolated Git worktrees for feature development, follows project directory conventions, verifies ignore rules, and checks the project baseline.
skill.summary: Create an isolated Git worktree with directory checks, project setup, and baseline test verification.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The 39 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, intended Git operations, documented worktree paths, and standard /dev/null redirection. Semantic review found automatic project code execution, an unapproved commit workflow, and a quoted-home-path defect.

remediation.issue: Setup and test commands can execute repository-controlled code automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Show the detected commands and require explicit approval before running package installation, build, or test steps.

remediation.issue: The workflow commits .gitignore changes without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before editing .gitignore and ask separately before creating a commit.

remediation.issue: The global path keeps the tilde inside quotes and prevents home expansion.
remediation.suggestion: Build the path from $HOME and verify that the resolved path is outside the repository.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow automatically runs dependency installation, build, and test commands. These commands can execute repository-controlled scripts without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to auto-detect and run package managers, builds, and tests. These tools commonly execute project-defined code.

semantic_findings.title: Unapproved Repository Commit
semantic_findings.description: When a worktree directory is not ignored, the workflow instructs the agent to change .gitignore and commit without requesting user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The numbered instructions explicitly require adding an ignore entry and committing it. No approval step is included.

semantic_findings.title: Quoted Home Path Becomes Project-Relative
semantic_findings.description: The quoted tilde remains literal in the path variable. The supposed global worktree can be created under the current project without ignore verification.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: POSIX shells do not expand a tilde inside double quotes. The quoted path is then passed directly to git worktree add.

content.value_statement: Branch switching can disrupt active work and mix unrelated changes. This skill creates an isolated Git worktree, verifies directory safety, runs project setup, and checks the test baseline.
actual_capabilities: Selects an existing project-local worktree directory using a defined priority.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a worktree directory preference before asking the user.
Verifies that a project-local worktree directory is ignored by Git.
Creates a new branch in an isolated Git worktree and enters that workspace.
Detects common project types, runs setup commands, and checks baseline tests.
limitations: Requires Git worktree support and a Unix-compatible shell.
Setup detection covers Node.js, Rust, Python, and Go project files.
Dependency installation and test commands can run project-controlled code.
The global path example needs tilde expansion correction before use.

use_cases.title: Develop a Feature in Parallel
use_cases.description: Create an isolated branch workspace while preserving the current working directory and its unfinished changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Urgent Hotfix
use_cases.description: Open a separate worktree for a hotfix without interrupting release preparation on another branch.

use_cases.title: Isolate Agent Implementation
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding workflow a dedicated workspace with directory checks and a recorded test baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated worktree for branch feature/login. Check existing directories, verify ignore rules, and report the final location.

prompt_templates.title: Follow Repository Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a worktree for branch fix/payment-timeout. Use the repository worktree convention, then ask before changing any tracked file.

prompt_templates.title: Verify the Project Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for refactor/cache. Detect the project type, show proposed setup and test commands, and request approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Global Isolated Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a global worktree for experiment/indexing. Resolve the location through HOME, confirm it is outside the repository, and preserve the current branch.

output_examples.input: Create an isolated worktree for the authentication feature.
output: Selected the existing project-local worktree directory.
Confirmed that Git ignores the directory.
Created the feature branch and reported the new workspace location.

output_examples.input: Prepare a worktree when no directory convention exists.
output_examples.output: The skill asks whether to use a project-local or global worktree directory before creating anything.

output_examples.input: Run the baseline check and the tests fail.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the failing baseline and requests a decision before feature implementation continues.

best_practices: Review and approve dependency installation and test commands before execution.
Confirm project-local worktree directories are ignored before creation.
Report baseline failures and obtain approval before feature work begins.
anti_patterns: Do not create a worktree inside an unignored project directory.
Do not treat a quoted tilde as the home directory in shell paths.
Do not commit ignore-file changes without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill delete worktrees?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on worktree creation and baseline verification. Cleanup requires a separate branch-finishing workflow.

faq.question: Can it use a global worktree location?
faq.answer: Yes. The global path should use HOME so the shell resolves the directory outside the repository.

faq.question: Does it support Windows shells?
faq.answer: The provided commands assume a Unix-compatible shell. Windows environments need equivalent path and command handling.

faq.question: Will it install project dependencies?
faq.answer: It detects common project files and proposes setup commands. Approval should be required before those commands run.

faq.question: What happens when baseline tests fail?
faq.answer: It reports the failures and asks whether to investigate or continue. It should not proceed automatically.

faq.question: Does it create a new Git branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented creation step adds a new branch while creating the isolated worktree.
